chunks: Ghayba of al-Tabarsi: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi al-Bilad who said:

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: What has become of the wretched Hamza ibn Bazi`? I said: He is here, he has arrived. He (peace be upon him) said: He claims that my father is alive? Today they are doubters, and tomorrow they will not die except upon heresy…

key_terms.الزَّنْدَقَةُ: Heresy, often specifically dualistic or hidden apostasy
key_terms.الشَّقِيُّ: The wretched one (a title of respect or specific identification)
key_terms.الشُّكَّاكٌ: Doubters, those who harbor doubt in faith
key_terms.حَمْزَةُ بْنُ بَزِيعٍ: Hamza ibn Bazi`, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: Who is Hamza ibn Bazi` and what did Imam al-Rida say about his state of belief?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Ghayba* highlights Hamza ibn Bazi` as a key figure in the early Shia discourse on the Imamate, specifically regarding the claim of his father's continued life (possibly referring to Imam Musa al-Kadhim or a specific theological stance). The Imam’s characterization of him and his contemporaries as 'doubters' (shakaak) who die upon 'heresy' (al-zandaqa) underscores the transition from simple doubt to entrenched heterodoxy during the Minor and Major Ghayba periods. This serves as a scholarly marker for distinguishing between those who merely questioned and those who adopted a distinct, opposing theological identity.
